# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Cigna — Appeals Department
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**From:** Cameron Alvarez
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

**RE:** Appeal of denial dated 2026-08-22
**Member:** Cameron Alvarez
**Member ID:** W878488198
**Reference number:** POC-58F5CA7616-94713
**Service denied:** Knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery, CPT 29881
**Governing policy:** Cigna CMM-312 Knee Surgery – Arthroscopic and Open Procedures V1.0.2026 (meniscus section), effective 2026-08-04 — https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-312%20Knee%20Surg%20Arthro%20%26%20Open%20Proc_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.20.2026.pdf

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of the knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery (CPT 29881) requested on my behalf by Dr. Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery. The notice dated 2026-08-22 states that the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking Cigna to reconsider that decision, because my records appear to match the plan's own published criteria in the policy named above. My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed.

Below I set out the plan's criteria, quoted from the policy, and the records submitted with the prior authorization request.

## 1. The imaging criterion

The policy states:

> "MRI or CT arthrogram shows a meniscal tear that extends to the articular surface (not simply degenerative changes, [i.e., fraying]) and correlates with the individual's reported symptoms and physical exam findings"

My MRI of the knee dated 2026-06-23 shows a **displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking**. That is a discrete, displaced tear — it is not described in my records as degenerative change or fraying. It also correlates directly with what I experience and with what my surgeon found: my records document locking and giving way, inability to squat or kneel, limitation to level walking, positive provocative testing on the affected side, and range of motion limited by pain.

## 2. The radiographic criterion

The policy states:

> "absence of Kellgren-Lawrence Grade II or greater findings on plain radiographs"

My imaging of 2026-06-23 documents **articular cartilage preserved, Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1**. Grade 1 is below Grade II.

The policy also provides:

> "Criteria exception: The absence of Kellgren-Lawrence grade II or greater findings is not required if there is the presence of a meniscal tear and a locked knee on physical exam."

My records document both a meniscal tear and mechanical locking, so this exception would also apply even apart from my grade 1 findings.

## 3. The symptom criterion

The policy states:

> "Symptoms include function-limiting knee pain and/or loss of knee function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment"

My records document 24 months of progressive knee pain, unrelieved by rest, with locking and giving way. I cannot squat or kneel, and I am limited to level walking. These are ordinary daily activities that I can no longer perform.

## 4. The conservative-care criterion

The policy states:

> "Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration"

My records document provider-directed non-surgical care as follows:

- **Supervised physical therapy**, focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, **14 weeks from 2026-04-08 to 2026-07-15, 20 visits completed**, documented in the physical therapy discharge note;
- **NSAIDs for 4 months** with inadequate relief;
- **Corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-01**, which gave 4 weeks of partial relief.

Despite all of this, my pain has been progressive and unrelieved by rest, and my knee continues to lock and give way.

The policy also provides:

> "Criteria exception: Three (3) months of provider-directed non-surgical management is not required if EITHER of the following conditions are present:"

and includes among those conditions:

> "meniscal tear with a locked knee on physical exam"

My records document a meniscal tear with mechanical locking, so this exception would also apply even apart from the conservative care I completed.

## 5. The physical examination criterion

The policy states:

> "Physical exam demonstrates at least TWO of the following findings:"

The excerpt I have ends in a colon and introduces a list that I have not been given in full. Two of the listed findings I do have are:

> "evidence of joint swelling/effusion"

> "positive Apley's compression test"

My records state that I have **positive provocative testing on the affected side** and **range of motion limited by pain**, along with documented locking and giving way. My records as I have them do not name each specific test by the wording the policy uses. If Cigna's determination rests on this criterion, I ask that you tell me in writing which exam findings on the plan's list were considered missing, so that Dr. Reyes can supply the specific examination detail from my chart. I am glad to have that documentation sent.

For the same reason, I want to be transparent: the excerpts of the policy available to me are partial, and some of them introduce lists of further conditions that were not reproduced. I am not able to quote every criterion the plan may have applied. The denial notice does not identify which specific criterion I failed to meet, and I am asking Cigna to identify it.

## What I am asking for

I ask that Cigna overturn the denial and authorize CPT 29881 as requested by Dr. Reyes. If the denial is not overturned, I ask that Cigna provide:

1. The specific criterion or criteria in Cigna CMM-312 Knee Surgery – Arthroscopic and Open Procedures V1.0.2026 (meniscus section) that my request was found not to meet;
2. The complete text of the criteria applied, including the lists that follow the provisions quoted above;
3. A free copy of all documents, records and clinical criteria relied on in making this determination;
4. The credentials and specialty of the reviewer who made this decision, and consideration of review by a physician board-certified in orthopedic surgery.

Please also treat this letter as my request to submit additional records, and let me know if anything further is needed from Dr. Reyes.

My denial notice states that my appeal must be received within 180 days of the notice date, by **2027-02-18**. I am submitting this appeal within that period. I understand appeals may be submitted through my.cigna.com using my plan's appeal form, or by calling 1-800-244-6224 or the number on my card, and that the correct mailing address is the appeal address printed on my denial letter, which I am using.

Thank you for taking another look at my case. I am living with a knee that locks and gives way, and I would like to get back to walking, working and moving normally.

Sincerely,

**Cameron Alvarez**

Reference number: POC-58F5CA7616-94713
